The Isle of Man TT: The Motorcyclist's Pilgrimage

The TT is the most famous motorcycle race in the world — a 37.73-mile circuit on closed public roads, with average lap speeds exceeding 135mph. For any motorcyclist, attending the TT is a bucket-list experience. Here's how to plan it.

When Is the TT?

The main TT festival runs for approximately two weeks in late May to early June. The 2026 dates should be confirmed on the official iomtt.com website. The schedule typically includes:

  • Practice week (Monday to Friday before race week)
  • Race week (the following week, with races most days)
  • Major races: Superbike, Supersport, Superstock, Senior TT, Sidecar

Getting There

  • Ferry: Isle of Man Steam Packet from Heysham, Liverpool, Dublin, or Belfast. Book as early as possible — TT sailings are announced in autumn for the following year and sell out fast.
  • Fly: Flights from major UK airports (Ronaldsway Airport). Book early for best prices. You can hire a motorcycle on the island from local dealers.

Accommodation

The island's accommodation sells out months in advance:

  • Hotels and B&Bs: The best options book 6-12 months ahead. Expect premium TT prices.
  • Camping: Several TT campsites operate during the festival. More affordable and with a great social atmosphere. Book early.
  • Homestays: Locals rent out rooms during TT. Check Airbnb and local accommodation sites.

Watching the Races

The TT is free to watch from anywhere around the 37.73-mile Mountain Course. Popular viewing spots:

  • The Grandstand (start/finish): Ticketed area with the best facilities and commentary.
  • The Bungalow: On the Mountain section at altitude. Bikes pass at extreme speed with mountain views behind.
  • Ballaugh Bridge: Riders launch off this humpback bridge — spectacular to watch.
  • Ramsey Hairpin: A tight corner in the town — close to the action.
  • Governor's Bridge: Near the grandstand. Riders attack the final corner at incredible speed.

Riding the Course

When roads aren't closed for practice or racing, the Mountain Course is a public road. You can ride the full 37.73-mile lap at legal speeds. It's an extraordinary experience — following the same road that the racers use at 200mph, at your own pace.

  • There is no speed limit on the Mountain Road section (outside the 30/40mph zones in towns)
  • Ride at your own pace — this is not a race. Respect other road users.
  • The Mountain section climbs to 1,400ft and can be foggy and cold even in June
The TT is more than racing — it's a festival of motorcycle culture. The paddock, the atmosphere, the fans, the evening events, and the shared passion of tens of thousands of riders create something unique. Even if racing isn't your thing, the TT is worth experiencing at least once.
keyTakeaways: The TT is a 37.73-mile circuit on closed public roads, with average lap speeds exceeding 135mph.
The main festival runs roughly two weeks from late May to early June, with practice week then race week.
Ferries via the Steam Packet sell out fast, so book as soon as sailings are announced in autumn.
Accommodation books 6-12 months ahead, with camping a more affordable and social alternative.
The course is a public road when not closed, so you can ride the full lap at legal speeds year-round.

faq.q: When is the Isle of Man TT held?
faq.a: The main TT festival runs for approximately two weeks in late May to early June, with 2026 dates confirmed on the official iomtt.com website. The schedule typically includes a practice week from Monday to Friday, followed by race week the following week with races most days, covering the Superbike, Supersport, Superstock, Senior TT and Sidecar classes.

faq.q: How do I get to the TT and when should I book?
faq.a: The Isle of Man Steam Packet ferry runs from Heysham, Liverpool, Dublin or Belfast, and you should book as early as possible because TT sailings are announced in autumn for the following year and sell out fast. Alternatively, fly into Ronaldsway Airport from major UK airports, booking early for the best prices, and hire a motorcycle from local dealers on the island.

faq.q: Where can I stay during TT week?
faq.a: The island's accommodation sells out months in advance. Hotels and B&Bs book best 6-12 months ahead and charge premium TT prices. Several TT campsites operate during the festival, offering a more affordable option with a great social atmosphere, so book early. Locals also rent out rooms during the TT, so check Airbnb and local accommodation sites.

faq.q: Where are the best places to watch the races?
faq.a: The TT is free to watch from anywhere around the 37.73-mile Mountain Course. The Grandstand at the start and finish is a ticketed area with the best facilities and commentary. The Bungalow on the mountain section offers extreme speed against mountain views, Ballaugh Bridge sees riders launch off a humpback bridge, and Ramsey Hairpin and Governor's Bridge put you close to the action.

faq.q: Can I ride the TT course myself?
faq.a: Yes. When roads are not closed for practice or racing, the Mountain Course is a public road and you can ride the full 37.73-mile lap at legal speeds, following the same road racers use at speed but at your own pace. There is no speed limit on the Mountain Road section outside the 30 and 40mph town zones, but ride sensibly, as the section climbs to 1,400ft and can be foggy and cold even in June.
